criteria.rationale: Examined L1 and L2. L1 is an accepted risk about implementer-written limits, mitigated by the brief listing them as data and by open findings blocking approval. L2 is verified: both plan digests cover accepted_limits. Neither is broader than its text; parser defects that alter a sealed limit are outside them (N2).

accepted_limits and limit are omitempty in the plan, bundle, both digests, drafts and attestations, and the digest test compares with the legacy bundle contract. within_limit_findings is an added field. Earlier brief templates stay selectable. The /11 text changed after round 8 was briefed with it; the template is unreleased and that run concluded changes-requested.

D1 and D2 address the stated cause, reviews that cannot converge without a declared environment: limits are sealed before review, classified by a distinct disposition requiring a sealed id and a reason, and disputable. The structural assessment reports no deltas to map.
Examined the ready check and decision gate messages: each names the limit, ADR or finding and the fault. Silent parser cases and missing text output are reported separately as N2, N4 and N5.

within-limit approves only an id present in the sealed bundle with a non-blank reason; blocker findings with a limit stay open; limit text is rendered as one quoted line with backticks neutralised; ADRs are read as regular bounded files without following links.

A spec section, two omitted-when-empty fields, one disposition and a lint check are close to the smallest sufficient change; a round cap would approve unreviewed work. The choice fails if sealed limits can differ from the declared ones, which N2 and N4 address.

findings.action: The spec declares 'modified: .pose/policy/delegation.json' (added by b5296a37), but the commits in the range that change it (7bf729e0, 3e1f03cf) carry no POSE-Spec trailer. 'artifact-check --spec pose-review-declared-threat-model --strict' and 'surface-check --strict' both exit 1 with error action-mismatch on that path, so two required tools fail. Attribute the exact revisions to the spec or correct the claim, then rerun both checks.

The continuation-line fix reads entry boundaries wrongly (probed through a test overlay). (a) A wrapped line starting with '#' ('see issue\n  #42 only on Linux') is taken as a heading: the limit is sealed cut at the first line, with no problem reported. (b) A nested '- only on Linux' sub-bullet is reported by lint, but the plan discards problems (line 134) and seals the limit without its qualifier. (c) A later non-indented paragraph after a blank line, or a following '* L2: ...' bullet, is appended into L1 and changes the sealed limit (L2 vanishes). (d) '- L1: no reason here', a blank line, then 'Some unrelated note. Accepted because other words follow.' now passes with no problem: the ready check accepts a reason borrowed from a later paragraph, which R4 and the round 4 rule refuse. End an entry where its Markdown list item ends, treat only real headings as headings, refuse (and do not seal) what cannot be read whole, with tests.

Regression from the N4 fix: the whole-slug pattern refuses a preceding '-', so an ADR that cites the spec only by its file link, for example '[it](../specs/2026-11-25-limited.md)', is no longer a citing ADR and the ready check demands no limit from it (probe returned no failure; the directory form and 'spec:limited' still demand L1). Dated flat files are how this repository's ADRs link specs, some by link alone with a descriptive label (.pose/adr/2026-09-21-federated-roadmap-acceptance-with-local-evidence-authority.md:6), so R4 goes unenforced for them. Recognise the dated spec path as a citation, with a test.

Fence and comment skipping is incomplete (probed). Any ``` or ~~~ prefix toggles one flag, so an example inside a four-backtick block or a ~~~ block holding ``` is sealed as a real limit; a 4-space indented code example is sealed too. A line starting with inline ```a``` or a literal unterminated '<!--' earlier in the body silently drops every later limit, with no problem and a passing lint (lint strips only closed comments); a comment written in backticks inside a limit is removed from its sealed text. A '* L1:' bullet alone is silently ignored.

within_limit_findings is counted and present in JSON, but the text output of the governance stats prints findings, accepted_risk, resolved, open and wont_fix without it, so the printed buckets still do not add up; review-check and closeout-check text still do not show within-limit findings, which the spec constraint wants visible in the closeout.

review-brief/11 still says in the conclusion step that a follow-up with action, owner and review_by is an accepted risk and 'any other finding stays open', which is false for a follow-up with a sealed limit (rule (m) states the exception only to rule (i)).

Carried from R8-N6: the lexical reason gate accepts placeholder words. Inside L1: it is a format gate over text the implementer writes, and the sealed brief shows that text for the reviewer to judge and dispute.
